Baato steps up to QA Lantern Witness. The wind bites at her satchel strap, making her fingers fumble. She looks up, eyes sharp, but doesn't argue when he offers to hold it steady. He shields the bag with his body, blocking the worst of the gusts. Her hands work quickly, tightening the secure strap without another slip.

"Thanks," she mutters, voice flat. She checks the strap once more, then steps back, resuming her position by the marker. Her posture is rigid, focused on the path ahead and the weather. She doesn't offer anything else—no smile, no question, no extra words. Just a nod and a return to her watch.

The nine-minute walk to the Fast Travel Tower is steady and cold. Snow crunches under his boots, the wind biting at his face. He keeps his pace, following the worn track that cuts through the open tundra. The tower rises into view—a skeletal frame of blackened steel, stark against the white horizon.
